newsitem.title: UK: IPE crude edges lower, awaits U.S. expiries.
newsitem.headline: IPE crude edges lower, awaits U.S. expiries.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures edged lower on Thursday, as the market remained wary ahead of U.S. product expiries, brokers said.
By 1120 GMT front month Brent was four cents lower at $18.93, but still well within reach of Wednesday's 8-week high of $19 a barrel.
"We're just retracing yesterday's gains a little. There's a bit of resistance around $19," one broker said. "But the market is bacilli treading water ahead of the U.S. product expiries."
Gas oil was 25 cents higher at $171.25 a tonne.
August unleaded gasoline and heating oil contracts expire on Thursday.

The spectre of an imminent rubber stamping of Iraq's aid distribution plan by the United Nations, expected to happen this week according to a UN spokesman, was also weighing on the market, brokers said.
But brokers were divided as to how New York would react to the expiries.
"It could go either way. We could see some more covering down on the gasoline, or it could all fizzle out," one broker said.
September Brent closed 38 cents higher on Wednesday at $18.97 a barrel, just three cents off the $19 high.
August gas oil closed $3.25 up on Wednesday at $171 a tonne.

Gas oil and crude on Wednesday advanced on the back of U.S. gasoline, which rallied strongly after U.S. Department of Energy and American Petroleum Institute stock data showed lower than expected gasoline stocks.
"I would expect to see a hesitation and a retracement after the expiry of the front month U.S. products," one broker said. "The market will be keeping a close eye on U.S. gasoline."
Production interruptions and increased demand during the busy summer driving season in the U.S. also helped to boost gasoline.
"I don't think that September will be as strong as the August contract," one broker said. "But I do think we'll start to see September pull away from the rest of the board."
